spring.definition: The season between winter and summer.

summer.definition: The warmest season of the year.

autumn.definition: The season between summer and winter.

winter.definition: The coldest season of the year.

dry-season.definition: A period in tropical or subtropical regions when rainfall drops sharply or stops, leaving mostly dry weather.

rainy-season.definition: One of the two main seasons in tropical climates, marked by frequent rainfall.

monsoon.definition: A seasonal wind in southern Asia.

equinox.definition: Either of two times of the year when the sun crosses the plane of the earth's equator and day and night are of equal length.

solstice.definition: Either of the two times of the year when the sun is at its greatest distance from the celestial equator.

harvest.definition: The gathering of crops when they are ready.

sunny.definition: Having plenty of sunshine and few clouds.

cloudy.definition: Covered with many clouds and little direct sunshine.

rainy.definition: Having or bringing rain from clouds in the sky.

snowy.definition: Having or bringing snow from cold clouds in the sky.

windy.definition: Having a lot of wind moving through the air.

foggy.definition: Covered by fog or containing thick fog.

stormy.definition: Having strong wind, rain, thunder, or lightning.

humid.definition: Containing or characterized by a great deal of water vapor.

thunder.definition: The loud sound that follows lightning.

lightning.definition: A bright flash of electricity in the sky.

tornado.definition: A violent column of air that spins around and moves across land.

hurricane.definition: A very powerful storm with strong winds that forms over the sea.

blizzard.definition: A severe snowstorm with strong winds and poor visibility.

hail.definition: Small balls of ice that fall from clouds during a storm.

flood.definition: A large amount of water covering normally dry land.

drought.definition: A long period with very little or no rain.

heat-wave.definition: A period of unusually hot weather.

ice-storm.definition: Freezing rain turns to ice when it lands, coating roads, trees, buildings, and other surfaces during a storm.

warm.definition: Having or producing a comfortable and agreeable degree of heat or imparting or maintaining heat.

cold.definition: Having a low or inadequate temperature or feeling a sensation of coldness or having been made cold by e.g. ice or refrigeration.

freezing.definition: The withdrawal of heat to change something from a liquid to a solid.

mild.definition: Moderate in type or degree or effect or force.

chilly.definition: Very hot and finely tapering pepper of special pungency.

boiling.definition: The application of heat to change something from a liquid to a gas.

below-zero.definition: Describes a temperature that falls below zero on the Celsius or Fahrenheit scale.

room-temperature.definition: Describes a substance or condition at the usual indoor temperature, without deliberate cooling or heating.

barometer.definition: An instrument that measures air pressure and helps predict weather changes.

weather-vane.definition: An instrument that points in the direction from which the wind is blowing.

rain-gauge.definition: An instrument that collects and measures rainfall.

anemometer.definition: An instrument that measures the speed of the wind.

weather-map.definition: A map showing weather conditions across an area during a news forecast.

forecast.definition: A prediction about how something (as the weather) will develop.

satellite.definition: A machine sent into space to collect information and send it back.

radar.definition: A system that uses radio waves to detect objects or weather.

weather-app.definition: A mobile or computer application that provides weather observations, forecasts, alerts, or related information.
weather-app.exampleUsage: The weather app showed a rain forecast.
